key_insight: Changing source-to-substrate distance (15–24 cm) measurably tunes the thickness, band gap, and semiconducting behavior of thermally evaporated CdTe, CdSe, and Sb2S3 thin films.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest SSD can be used as a practical process knob to optimize absorber-layer films for thin-film solar cells, especially CdTe and promising CdSe.
method: Thermally evaporated CdTe, CdSe, and Sb2S3 films at SSDs of 15, 18, 21, and 24 cm.
Characterized structure, composition, optics, and electrical behavior using XRD, EDX, optical analysis, and electrical measurements.
Estimated thickness with the envelope method and tracked band-gap changes with SSD.
evidence_signal: XRD and EDX confirmed phase/composition, optical measurements showed only marginal band-gap shifts with increasing SSD, and electrical tests indicated semiconducting films.
watch_item: The study is limited to laboratory-scale films and SSD tuning alone, so device-level performance and long-term stability still need validation before TFSC integration.
paper_title: Effect of Source-to-Substrate Distance on the Optical and Electrical Properties of Thermally Deposited CdTe, CdSe and Sb$_2$S$_3$ Thin Films
